cozumel.name: Cozumel
cozumel.summary: A Caribbean island off the Yucatán, best known for world-class reef diving and snorkelling.
cozumel.pier: Several piers sit south of San Miguel town; on very busy days some ships anchor and tender to downtown.
highlights: Reef snorkelling and diving along the west coast
The wild, windswept east coast beaches
cozumel.tip: Taxis use fixed fares by zone; ask the price first.

tips.pierToTown: Carnival and Royal Caribbean ships mostly use the pair of piers about two miles south of downtown San Miguel; on busy days some ships anchor and tender to the downtown docks. There's no public transit out of town: walk, rent a car or take a taxi (about M$30–60 within town).
tips.money: Prices are in pesos (M$); tourist spots also quote US$. Low-fee ATMs downtown: Banco Azteca, Banamex, Santander, Banorte. Tipping is like the US: 10–15% on meals. Bars may add 15% to the bill.
tips.food: Mayan and Yucatán specialties, like the slow, sweet-marinated Mayan pork at Casa Denis near the main square, the self-declared oldest restaurant in Cozumel.
tips.sight: San Gervasio, the island's most extensive Maya site, inland a few km north of the cross-island highway (car or taxi).
tips.safety: Pushy touts at the docks sell car rentals and tours; beware timeshare pitches. Most tourist accidents involve scooters, so rent one only if experienced. East-coast surf and undertow are dangerous. Fake silver: look for the .925 stamp; a magnet sticks to fakes.
tips.history: From about 1250 CE Cozumel was an important Maya port and pilgrimage centre. Juan de Grijalva's 1518 expedition was the first Spanish visit; Hernán Cortés stopped the next year.

george-town-cayman.name: George Town, Grand Cayman
george-town-cayman.summary: The capital of the Cayman Islands on Grand Cayman, compact and busy on multi-ship days.
george-town-cayman.pier: Ships anchor offshore and tender guests to the George Town waterfront.
highlights: Stingray City sandbar in the North Sound
Snorkelling right off the George Town shoreline
george-town-cayman.tip: Tender lines grow late in the day; head back early.

tips.pierToTown: There are no berths: cruise ships anchor offshore and tender passengers to the harbour dock in downtown George Town. Taxis wait at the docks. Seven Mile Beach is not within walking distance.
tips.food: The national dish is turtle stew, from the world's only green sea turtle farm. Restaurant food is expensive on Grand Cayman, even fast food.
tips.sight: Stingray City, the island's most famous excursion: feed and pet large rays in waist-deep water at the sandbar. In town, the National Museum is in the historic Old Courts Building (US$15).
tips.history: George Town, named after King George III, is the capital of the Cayman Islands. The remains of Fort George, built in 1790 to protect the harbour, stand on Harbour Drive.

roatan.name: Roatán
roatan.summary: The largest of Honduras' Bay Islands, set on an ancient coral reef with excellent diving.
roatan.pier: Ships use the piers near Coxen Hole and at Mahogany Bay; West Bay beach is a taxi ride away.
roatan.tip: Roads are winding and slow; budget extra return time.

tips.pierToTown: Cruise ships use Coxen Hole, the island's largest town, or Mahogany Bay outside French Harbour. At Mahogany Bay the lines discourage leaving the private beach compound except by taxi or tour.
tips.money: Prices of food, goods and services can double or more when cruise ships are in port; if you want to shop, it pays to wait until they leave.
tips.food: Seafood abounds: West End beach restaurants serve food of a very high standard, and a top quality lobster dinner can be found for around US$10.
tips.sight: Roatán Butterfly Garden: 15–20 species in a 3,000 sq ft enclosure, Sun–Fri 9 AM–5 PM, US$7 adults. Roatán has some of the best snorkel and dive spots in the Caribbean.
tips.history: The Bay Islands' first people were likely related to mainland tribes. Columbus visited neighbouring Guanaja on his fourth voyage (1502–1504), and the Bay of Honduras later drew settlers, pirates and traders.

philipsburg.name: Philipsburg
philipsburg.summary: The capital of Dutch Sint Maarten: duty-free shopping with a town beach right by the port.
philipsburg.pier: The cruise pier is a short walk or water-taxi ride along the bay to Front Street.
highlights: Maho Beach, where planes land just overhead
philipsburg.tip: The island is shared with French Saint-Martin; you can cross freely.

tips.pierToTown: Most visitors arrive at the A.C. Wathey cruise terminal, only a 10-minute walk from town. The Emmaplein bus terminal, the island's main one, is right where cruise and ferry visitors arrive.
tips.money: Shopping is duty free, and prices are often lower than on surrounding islands. Front Street is known for upscale jewellery and clothing shops.
tips.food: The boardwalk has many restaurants for lunch, several of which stay open after the cruise ships leave.
tips.sight: The boardwalk along Great Bay Beach, Front Street, and Fort Amsterdam. Old Street is an often-photographed alley between Front Street and Backstreet.
tips.history: Founded around 1733 by Scotsman John Philips to centralise trade. Fort Amsterdam and Fort Willem date from the 17th and 18th centuries; the boardwalk was built in 2006 for the growing cruise trade.

charlotte-amalie.name: Charlotte Amalie, St. Thomas
charlotte-amalie.summary: The capital of the US Virgin Islands on St. Thomas, a deep-water harbour town of steep streets.
charlotte-amalie.pier: Ships use Havensight or Crown Bay; downtown is a taxi or long walk away.
highlights: Ferry to St. John for snorkelling
charlotte-amalie.tip: Taxis charge per person; shared open-air taxis are common.

tips.pierToTown: Most ships dock at the West Indian Company Dock by Havensight Mall, nearly two miles from downtown; some use Crown Bay, a bit farther. Open-air "safari" cabs run to downtown for $4 per person each way.
tips.money: U.S. currency is used everywhere and ATMs are easy to find. Goods are imported duty free, so shopping is a big draw; check your customs allowance before buying.
tips.safety: Traffic drives on the left and most streets have no sidewalks. Taxis charge per person, so agree the price before you get in. At night, take taxis and avoid walking alone.
tips.history: Founded by the Danes in 1666 as Taphus ("tap house") and renamed in 1691 for Queen Charlotte Amalie, wife of King Christian V. Its deep harbour was once a haven for pirates, including Blackbeard.

san-juan.name: San Juan
san-juan.summary: Puerto Rico's capital, founded in 1521, with a walled, colourful old town.
san-juan.pier: Ships dock beside Old San Juan, so its streets and forts are right outside.
highlights: Old San Juan's blue cobbled streets
san-juan.tip: Old San Juan is hilly; wear good shoes.

tips.pierToTown: Cruise ships dock right by Old San Juan. A separate pier next to the old Pan American airport, used mostly by Royal Caribbean for turnarounds, must be reached by car or taxi.
tips.sight: The San Juan National Historic Site, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983, with the forts of El Morro and San Cristóbal, and La Fortaleza, the governor's home.
tips.safety: Old San Juan, Condado and Isla Verde tend to be very safe, with a 24-hour police presence in the Old City. Taxis have set rates between tourist zones and should use the meter otherwise.
tips.history: Juan Ponce de León founded the first settlement, Caparra, in 1508; the city on the islet was founded in 1521. El Morro repelled Drake and withstood the Dutch attack of 1625. It is the oldest city under U.S. jurisdiction.

ocho-rios.name: Ocho Rios
ocho-rios.summary: A lively resort town on Jamaica's north coast, packed with waterfalls and attractions.
ocho-rios.pier: Ships dock at two piers close to town; most sights are a short taxi ride away.
highlights: Turtle River Park and the town beach
ocho-rios.tip: Use licensed taxis (red PP plates) and agree the fare first.

tips.pierToTown: Two piers serve cruise ships. The main pier is nearest downtown, with vendors just outside the secure area. The James Bond pier farther west has almost no services and a long walk to town, but taxis line the sidewalk.
tips.food: Steamed fish at Fishermen's Beach, and jerk chicken: smoked spicy meat done over a spice wood fire.
tips.sight: Dunn's River Falls, 5 km from Ocho Rios. Fern Gully, a 3-mile gorge with over 540 varieties of fern, was formed by a 1907 earthquake.
tips.safety: Taxis called by hotels are safe but expensive; have one called for you rather than getting into an unmarked taxi.
tips.history: The Taíno called Jamaica Xamayca, land of wood and water. After Columbus landed in 1494, the Spanish named the area Las Chorreras (the waterfalls), probably the origin of the name Ocho Rios.

oranjestad.name: Oranjestad
oranjestad.summary: Aruba's capital, with Dutch-style buildings, a harbourside promenade and steady trade winds.
oranjestad.pier: The cruise terminal is in the heart of town beside the marina.
highlights: Downtown shops and the free tram
oranjestad.tip: Aruba is dry and sunny; bring sun protection.

tips.pierToTown: A tram links the cruise terminal with the city centre along the main street; tickets cost US$1. A taxi ride usually costs only US$8–15.
tips.sight: Fort Zoutman (1798), the island's oldest building, houses the Historical Museum of Aruba; you can climb the Willem III Tower ($15).
tips.safety: Crime is not much of a worry: locals don't pressure tourists into stores, and panhandlers are not an issue.
tips.history: European settlers set up modest plantations along Aruba's south coast from 1754, and urban development began around 1795–96 as trade restrictions eased.

nassau.name: Nassau
nassau.summary: The Bahamas' capital: a relaxed, low-rise city with pastel colonial buildings and a busy harbourfront.
nassau.pier: Ships berth at Prince George Wharf, right on the edge of downtown, so the centre is a short walk.
highlights: Bay Street shops and the Straw Market
Beaches across the bridge on Paradise Island or at Junkanoo Beach
nassau.tip: Agree taxi fares before you get in; many are set per person by zone.

tips.pierToTown: Up to seven ships dock at Prince George Wharf, next to downtown, and downtown distances are short enough to walk. Jitneys (minibuses) leave from Bay Street: $1, exact fare, until about 6 PM. Water taxi to Paradise Island from under the bridge: $6 round trip, until 6 PM.
tips.money: The Bahamian dollar is tied 1:1 to the US dollar, and US dollars are accepted everywhere at par; many shops give change in US$.
tips.food: Potters' Cay, under the Paradise Island bridge: stalls making fresh conch salad, conch fritters and other Bahamian seafood. Downtown holes-in-the-wall do fish, sides and dessert for around $8.
tips.sight: Fort Fincastle (1793), on a hill just south of town with cannons on display; tours daily 8 AM–3 PM. The 66-step Queen's Staircase, named after Queen Victoria, is beside it.
tips.safety: Licensed taxis have yellow plates; they rarely use the meter, so agree the fare first. Only ride licensed taxis: some criminals pose as drivers. Touts push jet-ski and booze-cruise trips. Most Cuban cigars sold here are fake.
tips.history: Founded in 1670 as Charles Town and rebuilt as Nassau in 1695. It became a pirates' den under Blackbeard until Governor Woodes Rogers restored British control from 1718.

freeport.name: Freeport
freeport.summary: The main town on Grand Bahama, a planned free-trade city still rebuilding after Hurricane Dorian (2019).
freeport.pier: The cruise port is outside town, so plan on a taxi or a tour to reach the beaches and shops.
highlights: Lucayan National Park's caves and beach
Snorkelling and quiet beaches along the south shore
freeport.tip: Check what has reopened since the hurricane before you set out.

tips.pierToTown: Taxis wait at the sea port. There is no such thing as a "service fee" or bag fee: you pay only the fare, plus a tip if deserved. Local minibuses cost $1 anywhere on the island and often wait until full.
tips.money: Bahamian dollars are equal in value to the US dollar, and US currency is accepted everywhere. Check your bill: some restaurants already include a 15% service charge; if not, 15% is the standard tip.
tips.food: Conch is the Bahamian classic: conch salad, citrus-infused and served cold; cracked conch, lightly batter-fried; and conch fritters with dipping sauce.
tips.sight: Port Lucaya Marketplace: duty-free shopping in over 80 stores overlooking the Bell Channel Bay marina. Nature lovers can head to the Rand Nature Centre or Lucayan National Park.
tips.safety: Areas that cater to tourists are heavily policed, but don't venture outside them alone. Ignore taxi drivers who ask for extra "fees".
tips.history: Freeport began in 1955, when the government granted financier Wallace Groves 50,000 acres of pineyard and swamp to develop as a free trade zone. It is now the second most populous city in the Bahamas.

bimini-bs.name: The Beach Club at Bimini
bimini-bs.summary: Bimini lies about 50 miles east of Miami; Virgin Voyages' adults-only Beach Club sits at Resorts World Bimini on North Bimini.
bimini-bs.pier: Ships dock at the Resorts World Bimini pier; free trams run every few minutes to the Beach Club.
highlights: Two lagoon-style pools with live DJ and pool volleyball
Private beach with loungers, daybeds and hammocks
Alice Town, North Bimini's main town, and Resorts World casino
bimini-bs.tip: Food, soda, water and Wi-Fi are included at the Beach Club; cocktails, cabanas and excursions cost extra.

celebration-key-bs.name: Celebration Key
celebration-key-bs.summary: Carnival's exclusive destination on the south side of Grand Bahama, opened July 19, 2025, with five themed 'portals' and more than 30 places to eat and drink.
celebration-key-bs.pier: Ships dock at a 2,200 ft pier that leads into Paradise Plaza and the 10-story Suncastle.
highlights: Starfish Lagoon: big family freshwater lagoon, Suncastle waterslides
Calypso Lagoon: DJ island, swim-up bar, swings bar (part 13+)
Lokono Cove: Bahamian-made goods; Pearl Cove Beach Club (18+, fee)
celebration-key-bs.tip: Mile-long white-sand beach; Pearl Cove, cabanas and excursions cost extra.

half-moon-cay-bs.name: RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay
half-moon-cay-bs.summary: Carnival Corporation's private island (Little San Salvador), between Eleuthera and Cat Island; only about 50 of its 2,400 acres are developed.
half-moon-cay-bs.pier: A new pier opened June 1, 2026, so Carnival ships now dock; Holland America guests still tender to the south side.
highlights: A long white-sand beach with free loungers and umbrellas
Horseback riding, including into the surf
half-moon-cay-bs.tip: Cabanas, daybeds and most excursions cost extra; the island is also an important waterfowl nesting area, so stay on paths.

perfect-day-at-cococay-bs.name: Perfect Day at CocoCay
perfect-day-at-cococay-bs.summary: Royal Caribbean's private island in the Berry Islands (Little Stirrup Cay), about 55 miles north of Nassau, rebuilt and renamed in 2019.
perfect-day-at-cococay-bs.pier: A pier on the north side lets ships dock directly; trams link Arrivals Plaza with the beaches.
highlights: Chill Island beaches and Oasis Lagoon, the Caribbean's largest freshwater pool
Thrill Waterpark with Daredevil's Peak and a wave pool (day pass)
Up, Up and Away helium balloon to 450 ft and a 1,600 ft zip line
perfect-day-at-cococay-bs.tip: Lunch at Chill Grill, Skipper's Grill and the Snack Shacks is included; Thrill Waterpark, Hideaway Beach (18+) and Coco Beach Club need paid passes.

princess-cays-bs.name: Princess Cays
princess-cays-bs.summary: Carnival Corporation's beach resort at the southern end of Eleuthera, used by Princess and Carnival; despite the name, it's not on separate islands.
princess-cays-bs.pier: Ships anchor offshore and tender guests to the beach.
highlights: Swimming and snorkeling off the beach
Kayaking, banana boats, parasailing and waverunners
Volleyball and basketball courts; cabanas to rent
princess-cays-bs.tip: US dollars are used; watersports and cabanas cost extra.

juneau-us.name: Juneau
juneau-us.summary: Alaska's capital, reachable only by sea or air, between mountains and the Gastineau Channel.
juneau-us.pier: Ships dock just south of downtown, an easy walk into town.
juneau-us.tip: Several thousand visitors arrive almost every day May–September; buses at the docks run to Mendenhall Glacier.

ketchikan-us.name: Ketchikan
ketchikan-us.summary: Alaska's 'First City' on the Inside Passage, known for totem poles and Creek Street.
ketchikan-us.pier: Ships dock right downtown; a free shuttle loops downtown and all berths in about 20 minutes.
highlights: Totem Heritage Center and Saxman totems
ketchikan-us.tip: The visitors bureau by berth 2 has free maps and tour info. Bring rain gear.

skagway-us.name: Skagway
skagway-us.summary: A Klondike Gold Rush town at the head of Lynn Canal, a few blocks wide and easy to walk.
skagway-us.pier: Ships dock at the edge of town; local SMART buses also run from the docks to Broadway.
highlights: Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park
skagway-us.tip: The White Pass round trip enters Canada, but you don't need a passport for it because you stay on the train.

sitka-us.name: Sitka
sitka-us.summary: Former Russian capital of Alaska on Baranof Island; the 1867 transfer to the US took place on Castle Hill.
sitka-us.pier: Most large ships dock at Old Sitka Dock, about 6 miles north; a free shuttle runs downtown. Otherwise ships anchor and tender.
highlights: Sitka National Historical Park totem trail
St. Michael's Cathedral and Castle Hill
sitka-us.tip: Allow time for the shuttle back from downtown.

icy-strait-point-us.name: Icy Strait Point (Hoonah)
icy-strait-point-us.summary: Alaska's only privately owned cruise destination, near Hoonah on Chichagof Island, owned by the Native Huna Totem Corporation.
icy-strait-point-us.pier: Cruise passengers arrive at the destination next to Hoonah.
icy-strait-point-us.tip: Huna Totem Corporation is owned by about 1,350 Alaska Natives with ties to Hoonah.

victoria-ca.name: Victoria
victoria-ca.summary: British Columbia's capital on Vancouver Island, with British-style architecture, Chinatown and First Nations culture.
victoria-ca.pier: Ships dock at Ogden Point, about 2.5 km southwest of the Inner Harbour; walk the waterfront or take a shuttle.
highlights: Inner Harbour and the Parliament Buildings
victoria-ca.tip: The cruise season runs April–October, with over 200 large-ship calls a year.

barcelona.name: Barcelona
barcelona.summary: Spain's second city and the capital of Catalonia: architecture, beaches and food.
barcelona.pier: Large ships dock 1-2 km southwest of the old town; a port shuttle runs to the Columbus monument.
highlights: The Gothic Quarter and La Rambla
barcelona.tip: Book Sagrada Família tickets ahead and watch for pickpockets.

tips.pierToTown: Large cruise ships dock 1–2 km southwest of the city; many lines run shuttle buses to the south end of La Rambla. The city is very walkable.
tips.food: Tapas are everywhere. A menu offering "tapes", the Catalan spelling, usually means a place locals use; skip the tourist tapas bars on the Barceloneta seafront for the backstreets.
tips.sight: The works of Antoni Gaudí, especially the Sagrada Família, Barcelona's symbol, are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
tips.safety: Pickpockets are common, and wallets and passports are favourite targets. Be wary of strangers who approach you in your language asking for help or a petition signature.
tips.history: Tradition credits Phoenician or Carthaginian settlers with founding the city; it was the Roman town Barcino more than 2,000 years ago. The 1992 Olympics turned it into a major tourist destination.

civitavecchia.name: Civitavecchia
civitavecchia.pier: A port shuttle takes guests to the gate; the train to Rome takes about an hour.
highlights: Rome's highlights by train or tour
civitavecchia.tip: Allow a large buffer for the train back to the ship.

tips.pierToTown: A free shuttle takes cruise passengers to the port entrance, within easy walking distance of shops and the train station. Regional FR5 trains run to Rome.
tips.food: The main street between the train station and the harbour has plenty of restaurants, pizzerias and bars at fairly low prices.
tips.sight: The 16th-century fortress built with the help of Michelangelo, and the National Archaeological Museum with finds from the Roman port.
tips.history: Emperor Trajan greatly enlarged the harbour in the early 2nd century, then called Centum Cellae. After Saracen raids, the town was rebuilt in 889 as Civitas Vetus, the "ancient town".

naples.name: Naples
naples.summary: An ancient, vibrant port city and a base for Pompeii, Vesuvius and the Amalfi Coast.
naples.pier: Ships dock at Stazione Marittima in the city centre near Piazza Municipio.
naples.tip: Trains to Pompeii are busy; start early.

tips.pierToTown: Cruise ships dock at the Stazione Marittima, a large terminal in the city centre near Piazza Municipio. Distances in the historic centre are small and easy to walk.
tips.food: Naples is the home of pizza: the art of the Neapolitan pizzaiolo is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list. Fresh mozzarella di bufala is also typical of the region.
tips.sight: The historic centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Pompeii and Herculaneum and Vesuvius, the only active volcano on the European continent, are nearby.
tips.safety: Only take licensed taxis: they have the city crest on the door and a meter, and must display set fares. Avoid the Quartieri Spagnoli and the Sanità after dark.
tips.history: Greek settlers founded Parthenope in the 8th century BC, and the town was refounded as Neapolis ("new city") in the 6th century BC. It is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

santorini.name: Santorini
santorini.summary: A volcanic island famous for cliff-top white villages over a flooded caldera.
santorini.pier: Ships anchor and tender to the old port below Fira; reach the top by cable car, steps or donkey.
santorini.tip: Cable car lines are long on busy days; tenders may pause in bad weather.

tips.pierToTown: Big ships anchor in the caldera west of Fira, and boats take passengers to the old port below the town. From there, take the cable car (€10 each way) or walk the 588 zigzag steps.
tips.sight: The caldera views and clifftop white villages, and the ancient ruins of Akrotiri and Thera. The Fira to Oia hiking trail is famous.
tips.safety: In bad weather, cruise ships may delay or cancel the shuttle boats. The steps up from the old port are narrow, slippery with donkey droppings, and shared with the donkeys.
tips.history: The Minoan eruption, about 3,600 years ago, was one of the largest in recorded history and left today's water-filled caldera. It is often linked to the legend of Atlantis.

mykonos.name: Mykonos
mykonos.summary: A lively Cycladic island with whitewashed lanes and windmills.
mykonos.pier: Most ships dock at Tourlos; a sea bus or shuttle runs to the old town.
mykonos.tip: The old town's lanes are a maze; save a pin to your meeting point.

tips.pierToTown: Almost all cruise ships dock at the new port in Tourlos, though some use the old port. A cruise shuttle bus runs to Mykonos Town, stopping near the northern bus station.
tips.food: Gyros, souvlaki and crepe shops all over town let you eat well for a few euros. Most restaurants post their prices at the entrance.
tips.sight: The windmills, built by the Venetians in the 16th century, and Little Venice, where houses' balconies hang over the sea. Delos, the ancient sacred island, is a short boat trip away.
tips.safety: Mykonos is generally safe; the main danger is drunk driving. Rent a motorbike or quad only if experienced, as roads are narrow and twisty.
tips.history: Herodotus says Carians first lived here, followed by Ionians from Athens. Neighbouring Delos, meeting place of the Delian League, made Mykonos a supply stop, though it was a poor island in ancient times.

dubrovnik.name: Dubrovnik
dubrovnik.summary: A historic walled city on the southern Adriatic coast.
dubrovnik.pier: Most ships dock at Gruž, 2.5 km from the Old Town; buses and taxis go to the Pile Gate. Some tender to the Old Port.
dubrovnik.tip: Walls get hot and crowded; go early.

tips.pierToTown: Cruise ships usually dock at Port Gruž, 2.5 km northwest of the Old Town; buses 1, 1A and 1B run there almost constantly. Some ships anchor offshore and tender straight to the Old Port.
tips.money: There are few ATMs outside the Old Town. Avoid Euronet machines in tourist areas, which may add fees.
tips.sight: The City Walls. Entry to the Old Town is free; you only pay to walk the walls. The Dubrovnik Pass, just €5 more, adds most museums and local buses.
tips.safety: A very safe city, but watch for pickpockets. Old Town streets are slippery, smoothed by centuries of footsteps.
tips.history: Probably founded in the 7th century as Ragusa by refugees from Epidaurum, it grew rich as the maritime Republic of Ragusa. It was besieged for seven months and shelled in 1991.

valletta.name: Valletta
valletta.summary: Malta's compact 16th-century capital, a UNESCO site on a peninsula.
valletta.pier: Ships dock at the Valletta Waterfront below the walls; a lift goes up to the city.
highlights: Grand Harbour views and the Three Cities
valletta.tip: The Barrakka lift saves the steep climb from the waterfront.

tips.pierToTown: The Barrakka Lift links the waterfront and the city level, 58 m in 23 seconds. The peninsula is only a couple of kilometres long and best explored on foot, though it's steep with stairs in places.
tips.sight: St. John's Co-Cathedral: plain outside, incredibly ornate inside, with a chapel for each langue of knights and a ceiling fresco by Mattia Preti. Mon–Sat 9 AM–4:45 PM, closed Sun.
tips.safety: Most petty crime against travellers happens in Sliema and St. Julian's rather than in Valletta. Electric mini-cabs in town charge at most €5.
tips.history: After the Knights Hospitaller won the Great Siege of 1565, Grand Master Jean de Valette laid the city's foundation stone on 28 March 1566. It is named after him.

palma.name: Palma de Mallorca
palma.summary: The capital of Mallorca and the Balearic Islands, with a striking cathedral.
palma.pier: Ships dock along the bay; buses and taxis reach the centre in minutes.
palma.tip: Summer heat is strong; sightsee early.

tips.pierToTown: The ferry port is 2 km southwest of the town centre. EMT city buses cost €2 within the city and €3 to the sea port, paid on board.
tips.sight: La Seu, Palma's vast cathedral, built on the site of a mosque; construction began in 1229 and finished in 1601. The Royal Palace of La Almudaina is next door.
tips.safety: Take great care of valuables: the town centre has plenty of pickpockets, and flower sellers and street touts may work with them.
tips.history: Founded as a Roman camp on a Talaiotic settlement, then held by the Byzantines and the Moors, who called it Medina Mayurqa, before James I of Aragon took it in the 13th century.

amsterdam-nl.name: Amsterdam
amsterdam-nl.summary: The Dutch capital of canals, museums and gabled houses.
amsterdam-nl.pier: Passenger Terminal Amsterdam, used only for cruise ships, is close to the city centre.
amsterdam-nl.tip: Canal cruises usually last one to two hours; you can also rent a pedal boat.

bergen-no.name: Bergen
bergen-no.summary: Norway's second city, between seven mountains, and one of Europe's busiest cruise ports.
bergen-no.pier: Bergen is one of Europe's busiest cruise ports; the centre is compact.
bergen-no.tip: It rains about 240 days a year in Bergen; bring a rain jacket.

copenhagen-dk.name: Copenhagen
copenhagen-dk.summary: Denmark's capital, with canals, palaces and the Tivoli Gardens.
copenhagen-dk.pier: The main cruise terminal is on Oceankaj in the north harbour; bus 27 runs to Østerport station.
copenhagen-dk.tip: Copenhagen is very bike-friendly; trains and metro are easy to use.

geiranger-no.name: Geiranger
geiranger-no.summary: A tiny village at the head of the Geirangerfjord, a UNESCO-listed fjord and Norway's second-busiest cruise port.
geiranger-no.pier: Ships use the pier and jetwalk; when more than one ship is in, you may tender.
highlights: Seven Sisters waterfall from the fjord
geiranger-no.tip: About 200 people live here but thousands visit daily; book tours early.

stockholm-se.name: Stockholm
stockholm-se.summary: Sweden's capital, spread over islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic.
stockholm-se.pier: Ships dock at terminals in the city; some calls use Nynäshamn, about 50 km south, so check yours.
stockholm-se.tip: Nynäshamn calls are linked to Stockholm by SL commuter train line 43.

tallinn-ee.name: Tallinn
tallinn-ee.summary: Estonia's capital, with one of Europe's best-preserved medieval old towns.
tallinn-ee.pier: From the Old City Harbour, the Old Town is about a 15–20 minute walk.
highlights: Old Town and Town Hall Square
tallinn-ee.tip: Town Hall Square's town hall is the oldest in the Nordic and Baltic countries.

helsinki-fi.name: Helsinki
helsinki-fi.summary: Finland's seaside capital, with neoclassical squares and Nordic design.
helsinki-fi.pier: Ships use various harbour terminals around the city; trams serve the main harbours.
helsinki-fi.tip: Ferries to Suomenlinna leave from Market Square.

cabo-san-lucas-mx.name: Cabo San Lucas
cabo-san-lucas-mx.currency: Mexican peso (US dollar often accepted in tourist areas)
cabo-san-lucas-mx.summary: A resort town at the southern tip of Baja California, where the Pacific meets the Sea of Cortez.
cabo-san-lucas-mx.pier: Ships anchor in the bay and tender guests to the marina.
highlights: El Arco (the Arch) and Land's End by boat
cabo-san-lucas-mx.tip: Ignore timeshare offers of free tours; the pitch can take up to 4 hours.

puerto-vallarta-mx.name: Puerto Vallarta
puerto-vallarta-mx.currency: Mexican peso (US dollar often accepted in tourist areas)
puerto-vallarta-mx.summary: A lively Pacific resort on Banderas Bay with a famous seaside Malecón.
puerto-vallarta-mx.pier: Ships dock at the Cruise Port, beside Marina Vallarta north of downtown; take a taxi or bus downtown.
highlights: Old Town and the Church of Our Lady of Guadalupe
puerto-vallarta-mx.tip: Agree taxi fares before you get in.

ensenada-mx.name: Ensenada
ensenada-mx.currency: Mexican peso (US dollar often accepted in tourist areas)
ensenada-mx.summary: A busy Baja California port on Todos Santos Bay, a common stop on cruises from Long Beach.
ensenada-mx.pier: Ensenada is a busy cruise port, visited by Mexican Riviera cruises from Long Beach.
highlights: Fish tacos and the fish market
ensenada-mx.tip: It's a popular weekend spot for Southern Californians, so it can be busy.

mazatl-n-mx.name: Mazatlán
mazatl-n-mx.currency: Mexican peso (US dollar often accepted in tourist areas)
mazatl-n-mx.summary: A Pacific port city in Sinaloa with a restored historic centre and a long seaside Malecón.
mazatl-n-mx.pier: Cruise ships dock at Mazatlán's busy port.
mazatl-n-mx.tip: Pulmonías, open-top taxis unique to Mazatlán, are everywhere; agree the price first.

progreso-mx.name: Progreso
progreso-mx.summary: A Gulf of Mexico port city in Yucatán, founded in 1811 to export sisal fibre.
progreso-mx.pier: Ships use the 6 km Muelle Altura pier, built long because the water is shallow.
progreso-mx.tip: Progreso is also the gateway to Mérida, inland.

belize-city-bz.name: Belize City
belize-city-bz.summary: Belize's largest city, on a small peninsula, and the capital until a 1961 hurricane led to a move to Belmopan.
belize-city-bz.pier: Cruise passengers arrive at the Tourist Village, which is open only when a ship is in town.
highlights: Old Belize at Mile 5 on the Western Highway
belize-city-bz.tip: Tours are timed to fit cruise port hours; book through the Tourist Village or your ship.

costa-maya.name: Costa Maya (Mahahual)
costa-maya.summary: A cruise port beside the small beach village of Mahahual on Mexico's quiet southern Caribbean coast.
costa-maya.pier: The port has its own shops and pools; Mahahual's beach strip is a short taxi ride or a longer walk.
costa-maya.tip: Ruins trips take most of the day; leave plenty of time to get back.

tips.pierToTown: The cruise ship dock (Puerto Costa Maya) is just up the beach from the village of Mahahual. A seaside malecon, a pedestrian walkway lined with restaurants and shops, runs along the beach to the south end of the village.
tips.money: The town has several ATMs, but they often don't work or run out of cash, so cash is still the best option.
tips.sight: Costa Maya is the closest port to lesser-known Maya ruins such as Chacchoben and Kohunlich. The further south from the cruise dock you go, the quieter the town becomes.
tips.history: Hurricane Dean, a Category 5 storm, hit just north of Mahahual in August 2007, heavily damaging the cruise dock and much of the village. Holland America's Westerdam was the first ship back, on October 31, 2008.

puerto-lim-n-cr.name: Puerto Limón
puerto-lim-n-cr.summary: Costa Rica's main Caribbean port, a regular stop for ships passing through the Panama Canal.
puerto-lim-n-cr.pier: Ships dock at the commercial port in town.
highlights: Boat trips to Tortuguero from nearby Moín
Rainforest canals where sloths are often spotted
puerto-lim-n-cr.tip: Buy souvenirs in town rather than from the tour company.
